questions.question: Refer-a-friend: you get a bonus when a friend joins. Your friend usually…
options: Often gets a bonus too, so check both sides' terms
questions.explanation: Many schemes reward both sides.

questions.question: A legit survey site will never ask you to…
questions.explanation: Paying to join is a red flag.

questions.question: A game app pays £15 if you reach level 30 in 14 days. It takes about 25 hours. Your hourly rate?
questions.explanation: £15 ÷ 25 hours = 60p an hour.

questions.question: A survey site pays 40p per survey with a £5 minimum cash-out. Half your attempts get screened out. Roughly how many attempts to cash out?
questions.explanation: You need 13 completed surveys, so about 25 attempts.

questions.question: Survey A pays £1 for 10 minutes. Survey B pays £2.50 for 30 minutes. Which pays more per hour?
questions.explanation: A is £6/hour, B is £5/hour.

questions.question: Survey sites typically pay…
options: A few pence to a couple of pounds per survey
questions.explanation: It's pocket money for spare minutes.

questions.question: Before putting hours into a rewards app, check…
options: The minimum cash-out and recent payout reviews
questions.explanation: Some apps set cash-outs high enough that few people reach them.

questions.question: What helps you sell unwanted items faster and for more?
options: Clear photos and an honest description
The highest price you can think of
questions.explanation: Good photos and honesty build trust.

questions.question: What's the honest way to share referral codes?
options: Share where the rules allow, never spam or fake reviews
questions.explanation: Spam gets codes banned and communities annoyed.

questions.question: Using fake or duplicate accounts to claim referral bonuses is…
options: Against the terms, can be fraud, and leads to clawbacks or bans
Fine if the amounts are small
questions.explanation: Companies check for duplicate accounts.

questions.question: You miss a play-to-earn milestone deadline by one day. Usually you get…
questions.explanation: Deadlines are strict, so check them before you start.

questions.question: A “mystery shopper” job sends you a cheque to cash, asking you to wire part of it back. This is…
questions.explanation: The cheque bounces later and you lose the money you sent.

questions.question: Paid online surveys typically pay:
options: Small amounts per survey, so they suit spare minutes rather than serious income
questions.explanation: Surveys are low-pay but easy; treat as pocket money, not a job.

questions.question: Selling your unwanted items online earns best when you:
options: List everything at once at high prices
Price realistically, photograph well and include postage in your thinking
questions.explanation: Speed of sale beats maximum price for clutter; good photos double response.

questions.question: A buyer offers to overpay you and asks you to refund the difference. This is:
options: A classic overpayment scam; the original payment will reverse
questions.explanation: Never refund 'overpayments'; block and report.

questions.question: Selling locally for cash vs posting: posting to strangers needs:
options: Payment protection, like platform-managed payments, not direct bank transfer to unknown buyers
questions.explanation: Platform payments offer some recourse; direct transfers to strangers often don't.

questions.question: Making money from surveys and apps requires declaring income above:
options: The £1,000 trading allowance per tax year
questions.explanation: Total self-employment income above £1,000 needs declaring; small amounts under it don't.

questions.question: Getting paid to write fake reviews is:
options: Illegal and undermines trust; platforms and the law treat it as deceptive
questions.explanation: Fake reviews are banned practice; they can get you and the seller in real trouble.

questions.question: Sharing referral links is most effective and honest when:
options: Shared genuinely with people who'd actually benefit, with disclosure that you earn
questions.explanation: Disclosure is required by ad rules and builds trust that makes referrals work.

questions.question: Play-to-earn and reward apps realistically deliver:
options: Small rewards for significant time, so check the effective hourly rate
questions.explanation: Most reward apps pay pennies per hour; a few pay well; always compute your effective rate.

questions.question: A tutoring side income can be scaled by:
options: Group sessions or recorded materials, raising hourly value over time
questions.explanation: Trading hours has a ceiling; leverage (groups, courses) breaks it.

questions.question: Before buying equipment for a side hustle, you should:
options: Validate demand cheaply first, borrowing or renting before owning
questions.explanation: Validate first; equipment bought before demand is a common small-business trap.

questions.question: A digital product (template, guide, course) differs from selling hours because:
options: It can sell repeatedly without more of your time
questions.explanation: Products decouple income from hours, which is the whole point of building assets.

questions.question: The safest way to take payments for a small side business is:
options: A platform with buyer/seller protection or a proper payment account
questions.explanation: Protection rails cost small fees and prevent the classic 'I've paid, send it' scam.

questions.question: If a 'side income opportunity' requires recruiting others to earn, it is likely:
options: A pyramid or MLM structure, where most participants lose money
questions.explanation: Earnings that depend on recruitment rather than product sales are the MLM signature.

questions.question: A realistic first target for a side income build is:
options: Something small and repeatable, like £50-£100/month, then compounding what works
questions.explanation: Small, repeatable, real beats big, imaginary, never. Scale what works.

questions.question: Money earned from side income should ideally be:
options: Partly reinvested or saved, so the side income builds assets
questions.explanation: The point is building assets; paying yourself some and reinvesting the rest compounds it.

questions.question: Selling services (design, writing, repair) needs:
options: Clear scope and payment terms agreed in writing before starting
questions.explanation: Written scope and terms prevent the classic 'scope creep and no payment' spiral.

questions.question: A side hustle that survives is usually one that:
options: Fits your existing skills and schedule, with demand you've verified
questions.explanation: Fit and verified demand beat novelty; most failed hustles skipped the demand check.

questions.question: Income from gig platforms (delivery, rides) is:
options: Taxable self-employment income; platforms report data to HMRC increasingly
questions.explanation: Gig work is self-employment: register above the allowance, track mileage and costs.

questions.question: Tracking expenses for a side business matters because:
options: Allowable expenses reduce your taxable profit, so good records mean paying less tax legitimately
questions.explanation: Mileage, materials, platform fees and home office use can all count; no records, no relief.

questions.question: A simple way to separate side income is:
options: Mixing it into your main account
A separate account or pot for side income, costs and tax set-aside
questions.explanation: Separation makes tax time trivial and shows whether the hustle really pays.

questions.question: Before signing up to any 'get paid to' platform, check:
options: Reviews on independent sites, payout thresholds, and how people actually get paid
questions.explanation: Payout reliability is the whole game; many platforms never pay out in practice.

questions.question: Someone offers you £200 to receive money into your bank account and forward it. This is:
options: Money muling, a money-laundering crime that can get your bank accounts closed and a criminal record
questions.explanation: Money muling is serious crime with lasting consequences, however innocent it's made to sound.
